Cause: distractor sets built by iterating ONE operation on a seed (a doubling ladder, a radius-vs-diameter family), so the ladder is visible without the stem and the key is the middle rung. Authoring rule: the four distractors must come from DIFFERENT operations. Also recorded: with ascending numeric options and a key that is never rank 5, the key-letter spread check and the rank check measure the same thing, so a clean letter spread is weaker evidence than it looks. spec.method: hand-authored, solve-gated; four distractors from FOUR DIFFERENT operations, never one operation iterated

batches.note: Attack margin +8.3 (33.3% vs 25.0% control), best solver 41.7%. SSAT math 96 -> 108 against a 50-item section, closing the last gap: EVERY delivered section of both tests now clears two full forms. Written against the defect that dropped six items from s4 - distractor sets built by iterating ONE operation on a seed, so the ladder and therefore the key were visible without the question. The attacker enumerated every pairwise relation across all 12 sets and found no chain of one operation through three or more options; the longest runs are two-member pairs. UNRESOLVED, recorded rather than acted on: the attacker proposed a HUB pattern - four distractors from four different operations still leak if all four derive FROM the key, making it the unique referenced value (SM5-02, SM5-06, SM5-12). Measured 33.3% against 20% chance on 9 picks, which is not significant at that size. Worth re-testing when the cohort is larger; the fix would be to relate some distractors to each other or to an intermediate quantity rather than all to the key. n=12 is small and the attacker said so itself, declining to trust any accuracy figure at that size and trusting only the ladder finding, which is arithmetic and was checked exhaustively rather than sampled.

Also recorded: about half the batch turns on one underlying decision (is the blank the finite verb, and what is its number) — 13 items across two overlapping templates — and the passages cluster five-to-a-topic (bees, surveying, ocean biology, 19th-century medicine).

NOT OVERRIDDEN — the two R&W batches on 2026-09-04 failed this same stage and shipped under BANK_GATE_OVERRIDE, recorded there as "a judgement call, not a clean pass". Making that call twice by myself is how a bar becomes decorative.

IV10-30 dropped unanimously — the stem said the shop "happens to sit" on the corner, which marks fortuity, so "luck" was defensible against "location"; one word fixes it. IV10-07 and IV10-18 dropped on majority-weak distractors.

shape.verdict: Helper gate passed 30/30 (4 distinct choices including the key, non-empty prompt and explanation). Letters A8/B8/C7/D7, 0 of 27 sliding windows of four a permutation, letter x length-rank r = 0.083. Dedupe: 0 exact and 0 near-duplicate (Jaccard >= 0.40) against 259 prior items across 8 sibling files; 2 key-word collisions found and rekeyed. RECORDED LIMITATION, measured by the author rather than assumed: an exhaustive promotion sweep put all 90 wrong keys through the structural gate and 56 SURVIVED, with all 34 refusals coming from the letter-spread check reacting to the slot moving. There is no arithmetic gate on a verbal batch, so structural green is not evidence the keys are right — only the with-source grade reaches that.

withsource.verdict: Three independent graders, each confirming the file sha256 before starting (211b6d04782c). Keys agreed 3/3 on 30 of 30 — no unreachable key. 27 survive. All three re-read every explanation against the FINAL stem and option text and all three found NO stale referent, the recorded defect on this family; one mechanical check confirmed every explanation names all four of its own options and no word that is not an option. IV10-30 drew a non-exclusive vote from all three, each reaching the same argument independently. Difficulty medians easy 7 / medium 12 / hard 8.

nosource.verdict: Options-only, stem stripped, keys dealt flat, three solvers: 20.0 / 13.3 / 16.7, pooled 16.7% — BELOW the 25.0% chance line. Pooled confident subset 6 of 40 = 15.0%. The solvers agreed with EACH OTHER on 21-25 of 30 and were agreeing on the wrong option: all three named the rule "three options cluster on one axis, the odd one out is the key", and the batch is built the other way round, so the attractive singleton is a distractor and the key wins only on the sentence. Strongest authoring result measured in this repo.

elimination.verdict: PASSES. Rule is zero items with any confidently rejectable option. Three solvers, all 30 items, all 120 options: legal==1 on 0 of 90 votes, any legal<4 on 0 of 90. All three reached it independently and by the same reasoning — a bare lexical option carries no proposition to contradict, no set holds a synonym or subsumption pair (the near-misses are ANTONYM pairs, which kill nothing), and every option is a well-formed completion of some stem. Each explicitly refused to count the cluster/singleton shape as an elimination, recording legal:4 and calling it a lean.

tells.verdict: The singleton inversion was MEASURED rather than argued. The three elimination solvers deliberately bet against the singleton on every item and scored 26/90 = 28.9%, against the original singleton rule at 16.7% and a 33.3% ceiling for picking uniformly from the three cluster members. So the axis carries real information — inverting gains 12.2 points over the singleton rule — but a student who learns the inversion gains only +3.9 over chance and lands well short of the ceiling, meaning that within the cluster there is no signal at all. Recorded as a batch-level shape with no automated guard, of the same family as the "identical key prose across lectures" case, and fed forward to s11: the inversion should not be this consistent across a whole form.

batches.note:
ACT Reading, 18 items in 2 passages (a PAIRED natural_science pair — the first paired items in that genre, which previously held 0 of the bank's 36 — and a literary_narrative). STAGED verified=false, following act-reading-v4. The assembler ignores it until a human sitting flips it.

SHA REBOUND 2026-09-12 (was aff2e8a96992, now 11540242c4db). The file moved after it was graded and the entry went stale; the register flagged it as needing "a fresh grade or an explanation before it is flipped". This is the explanation, and it was checked field by field rather than asserted. Diffing the graded revision (6ce25ed4) against the current file: 18 items both sides, no ids added or removed, and the ONLY field that differs anywhere is `difficulty`, on 6 items. Items whose grader-visible content changed -- passage, prompt, choices, correct_answer, passage_id, domain -- is ZERO. The relabel is the graders' own medians being written back: author 4 easy / 9 medium / 5 hard -> 4 / 12 / 2, which is exactly what the register recorded and which reproduces on the two files. So the key and exclusivity grade stands; no regrade is owed. NOTE that difficulty is not inert -- assembleFromBank treats the band as a preference within a domain -- but it is not something a grader read or keyed, and the new labels are the graders' own.

P1-Q9 REPAIRED 2026-09-13 (sha 11540242c4db -> c7012ff79cdf). TWO GRADERS NAMED THIS ITEM INDEPENDENTLY WITH THE SAME ONE-WORD FIX and it is now applied. The key read "Sound is produced only while an AVALANCHE is in motion", while Passage B's whole opening produces booming with no dune and no avalanche -- eight centimetres of poured sand sheared in a chute. Reaching the key meant treating 'avalanche' and 'shear' as interchangeable, which Passage B spends a paragraph separating, and THE EXPLANATION'S OWN PARENTHETICAL CONCEDED IT: "which is what an avalanche does". Key is now "only while the SAND is in motion" and the explanation says plainly that what the two passages share is motion, not an avalanche. The three distractors are untouched and each still fails on its own passage evidence (Passage A booms at 51cm and at 29cm, so no thinning requirement; Passage B's formula covers a range of diameters; Passage B booms on a chute with no damp bed). The option set keeps its parallel "Sound is produced only while X" frame, which a grader specifically called the CLEAN shape. No rival option becomes defensible, so this removes a reason to reject all four rather than changing which option wins.

THIS DOES NOT CLEAR THE BATCH. `tells` remains FAIL and the reason is unchanged: three graders independently found 3 of 9, 3 of 9, and 2-decisive-plus-2-assisted paired items answerable from SUBJECT RECALL, which is a property of the topic and not of this item. That still needs a person, asked the targeted question -- did you recognise the subject, and did it decide any pick?

shape.verdict: act-bank-helper check reading: 18 items in 2 passages, 9 and 9 against PER_PASSAGE.reading = 9, structure OK. Domain mix KID 9 (50.0%) / CS 5 (27.8%) / IKI 4 (22.2%), all three inside the blueprint bands 44-52 / 26-33 / 19-26. Genre choice was driven by measured gaps, not taste: natural_science was the ONLY genre with zero paired items, so no form could ever pair its natural-science slot; literary_narrative was the only genre whose Integration share (16.7%) sat below the 19-26% band. Author ran 28 break-tests, 12 planted defects refused and 4 benign controls passed, and attacking the harness found two real defects in the author's own checker — a 5-choice item passing silently against an assumed 4-option control, and a key absent from choices "caught" via undefined incrementing a NaN bucket that fails every threshold. Both now exit 2 without returning a number.

withsource.verdict: Three independent graders, all three reporting the SAME file hash (aff2e8a96992) before and after. 18 of 18 keys agreed 3/3. ZERO non-exclusive votes from any grader — one explicitly tried to spend a drop on P1-Q9 and could not justify it. Difficulty medians 4 easy / 12 medium / 2 hard against the author's 4/9/5: all three read the batch easier than authored, and all three named P2-Q9 as the item to rewrite if the form needs another hard, because its key paraphrases the final paragraph nearly word for word.

nosource.verdict: NOT RUN, AND DELIBERATELY SO — recorded as a non-measurement rather than a pass. On ACT Reading this instrument cannot discriminate: the model floor is about 83% and a human-CLEARED form scored 83.3%, so a number here separates nothing. Tuning to it would be fitting to noise. The gate is the human sitting, which is why this cohort stages verified=false. Do not read this stage as evidence.

elimination.verdict: Author ran an exhaustive promotion sweep over all 72 option positions — 18 keys and 54 distractor promotions — against the option-set proxies: real keys flagged 0/18, distractor promotions flagged 0/54. The SYMMETRY is the load-bearing part: if keys never fired while distractors often did, then "the key is the one that is NOT the odd one out" would be a free rule. Per-item legality was rebuilt to 4-of-4 on all 18 across three repair rounds; eight items were not 4/4 on first draft and were redesigned, including one whose key was the only option naming both disputed quantities (an axis-alignment leak) and one whose key was an act of judgment among three named sounds (a kind-singleton).

tells.verdict: FAILS, on a defect no structural check can see and the attack cannot reach: SUBJECT RECALL. All three graders volunteered it unprompted and independently. The author chose booming dunes because there is no scientific consensus to recall, and all three confirmed that premise is CORRECT and is not what protects an item — what protects it is whether the key coincides with the prior. The two rival accounts (a dry-layer acoustic waveguide over a denser substrate; shear-rate x grain-diameter collision synchronisation) are each well documented, and the batch assigns one camp per passage, so recognition routes by camp without any consensus existing. Counts: grader A 3 of 9 outright plus 2 partly, grader B 3 of 9, grader C 2 decisive plus 2 assisted. All three name P1-Q4 and P1-Q9 in the cluster. One grader notes that P1-Q9s option set is the CLEAN shape — four parallel "Sound is produced only while X" frames varying one term — so the leak there is recall, not axis-alignment, and a cheap structural check would never see it. Two graders also named the same single wording fix, independently: P1-Q9s key says "only while an AVALANCHE is in motion" while Passage Bs opening produces booming with no dune and no avalanche at all, eight centimetres of poured sand sheared in a chute; the explanations own parenthetical concedes the gap. "while the sand is in motion" costs nothing. Also flagged: P1-Q8s three non-keys describe concessions Passage A never makes anywhere, collapsing a cross-passage task into locate-the-detail.

withsource.verdict: Three graders on the sanitized render, all reporting sha 0cc729e6e5804c24 before and after. 28 of 28 keys agreed 3/3, ZERO non-exclusive votes, none guessed. All three credited the same two stems for closing ambiguity that usually bites: AM8N-05's "all positive terms" kills the r = -3/2 branch, and AM8N-23 is safe only because neither endpoint of "between 20 and 150" is a multiple of 7. DIFFICULTY: the author claimed 8 hard and all three graders found 4 — the SEVENTH consecutive batch whose author count failed independent grading. Unanimous on AM8N-14, -22 and -27; two of three also named -13. Two graders independently flagged AM8N-14 as recall-gated rather than insight-gated (you either know det(kA) = k^n det A or you do not) and asked for it to be counted separately, which is a distinction worth keeping.

nosource.verdict: Options-only attack, 3 solvers: 31.0% vs 25.0%, margin +6.0. 2 items solved by all three (AM8N-21, AM8N-24). ALL THREE SOLVERS MEASURED THE NULL PER CHANNEL before reporting anything, one against two nulls (uniform over the item's own range, and a pooled draw from the batch-wide option values, which is the harder test because it draws real exam-shaped numbers). Their agreed verdicts: geometric run middle 4 of 25 against 0.17-0.31 expected = REAL, p ~ 4e-5; key-is-product 2 of 25 against 0.13-0.34 = REAL, p ~ 1e-2; arithmetic run middle 4-5 against 2.5-3.0 = NOISE; pair-sums-to-a-constant 3 against 1.8-1.9 = NOISE. Three pair-sums (47+43=90, 24+336=360, 72+18=90) and five arithmetic runs would each have read as a finding on a raw count, and all three solvers reported them as nothing. One added a domain check on top: Number and Quantity supplies no angle or percentage constant, so a 90-sum there is meaningless whatever its p-value — the configuration has to make the constant mean something.

tells.verdict: The exact checkers report: run-middle 5 items carry the shape with the key at the middle on 0; pair-constant 0 of 25 scorable; key-is-sum 2 sum nodes with the key in 0; formula-options zero population. THE NON-NUMERIC SETS SPLIT, and all three solvers reached the same reading independently. AM8N-07 {1, i, -1, -i} is the COMPLETE CLOSED SET of the powers of i — every member equally reachable, nothing distinguished by form — and all three called it the model shape for this domain. AM8N-24 {3+i, 1-3i, 1+3i, 2+6i} is NOT closed, and two solvers called it a derivational hub in complex form: 1+3i has its conjugate, its double and its component-swap as the other three, so all three distractors are visibly manufactured from one option. It is one of the two items solved by all three. AM8N-21 (matrix dimensions in words) puts a transpose pair adjacent, which narrows four options to two for free; two solvers declined to call that confidence and marked it a guess. Both leaking items are recorded as REPAIR CANDIDATES rather than dropped: at +6.0 with every exact channel clean, the uniform drop rule selects nothing.

batches.note: 28 items, SSAT Upper Level Quantitative, FIVE choices. NOTHING DROPPED. The attack came in at +6.2 with two items solved by all three solvers — but all three filed ZERO confident picks and both items are declared guesses in their own words (neutral rotation pick; nothing fires; guess), against 0.50 expected at the run rate, p ~ 0.09. Per the clause this run added to the brief (3d-bis), unanimity among declared guesses is not evidence and triggers no drop. Every exact checker is clean. BANK_BAND=mixed.

withsource.verdict: Three graders on the sanitized render, all reporting sha 076456f976dfefb9 before and after. 28 of 28 keys agreed 3/3, ZERO non-exclusive votes, none guessed, and all three confirmed every item is hand-sized without a calculator. DIFFICULTY: author claimed 8 hard, graders found 4, 4 and 3 — the eighth consecutive cut, and all three named S13-21 and S13-27 as genuinely hard and worth keeping. STRICT was 4 / 7 / 4, and one grader flagged their own cliff — their strict group of 4 breaks to 0 if find-a-rate and scale-to-n-units count as distinct procedures, which they reported rather than hid. Both previous-batch defects confirmed ABSENT: no mathematics spelled out in prose without grouping (all three attacked the candidate expressions and found no second reading landing on a listed option), and no combinations by formula.

nosource.verdict: Options-only attack, 3 solvers, FIVE-wide against a 20.0% line: 26.2%, margin +6.2. ALL THREE FILED ZERO CONFIDENT PICKS. Each measured the null twice and one of them corrected the project method in the process: a uniform-range null made the run channel read 13 observed against 3.57 expected, a 3.6x finding, while a null resampling from the multiples of the item own gcd gave 8.26 expected and p = 0.010 — because real option sets are round numbers sharing a unit, not uniform draws. Under the correct null the pair-sum and key-as-sum channels sit BELOW chance. Two solvers independently agreed the author count of 11 run middles is right and both declined to bet either direction, one on decision-theoretic grounds: betting against the middle across 11-13 items is worth +0.65 expected items if right and -2.6 if wrong.

tells.verdict: check-run-middle: key is the middle on 0. check-option-pair-constant: key in the pair on 0 (control 50.0%). check-key-is-sum: key is a sum node on 0, product nodes 0. A solver attacked the hub channel rather than reporting it — it was the largest gap at 12 fired against 2.63 expected, but widening the simple-ratio list from 12 ratios to 38 kept the elevation while CHANGING WHICH OPTION IT NAMES on nearly every item, so a channel whose named option is a function of a free parameter cannot support a pick. What the elevation measures is that this author builds distractors as simple multiples of the key, which is sound practice. RECORDED FOR REPAIR, NOT DROPPED: one grader found four items with options eliminable by magnitude without doing the work — S13-09 (three of five exceed what more than 4 people must need), S13-14 (three exceed the perimeter), S13-28 (two exceed the stated class of 30), S13-18 (two impossible for a mean of 80-95). The pattern concentrates in easy items where a raw intermediate value was reached for as a fifth option.

batches.note: 28 items, ACT Math Algebra, NOTHING DROPPED. Commissioned at the MEASURED binding domain rather than from memory: form-capacity showed ACT Math capped at 7 forms by Algebra (60 live items, ~8 per form). That premise was then nearly invalidated by the tool itself -- the author re-ran form-capacity to check its own brief and got 401, 428 and 152 items on three runs, because pageAll used .range() with no .order(); the binding domain read as Number and Quantity on the bad run. Fixed before this batch was trusted. BANK_BAND=mixed. THREE PROMPTS WERE EDITED AFTER THE WITH-SOURCE GRADE and the reasoning is recorded rather than hidden: AM9A-26 used a lowercase x as the multiplication sign in a batch where x is the variable (all three graders flagged it), AM9A-22 stated money in dollars with bare numeric options, AM9A-21 carried an "x is a positive number" clause on a linear equation with a unique root. None changes an answer, and all three graders solved all three items correctly and exclusively under the OLD, strictly more ambiguous wording -- so the grade holds a fortiori. A script asserted that no choices array and no correct_answer moved, and the options-only render rebuilt byte-identical (blind sha 20cb752540d6d315), so the nosource verdict stays bound to the same option strings.

The author ran an exhaustive break-test -- 84 promotions refused, plus a rigged control that correctly survived, so the harness can report a survivor. SIX DEFECTS THE AUTHOR FOUND IN ITS OWN DRAFT, four beyond any repo checker: a key equal to the product of two distractors; a numeric hub opening at +8.3pts, fixed by REPLACING a structurally unfixable discriminant item rather than shuffling its numbers; its own duplicate checker returning jaccard 1.00 on non-identical stems because word tokenisation deletes digits and symbols, rewritten on character 4-grams with a self-test; and that rewrite then finding TWO REAL NEAR-DUPLICATES OF LIVE ITEMS (an x+1/x identity already in act-math-v7-alg, an overtime-pay item with the same numbers as one in act-math-v1), both replaced. Also flagged: check-explanation-option-refs and check-explanation-ordinals accept a file argument and silently ignore it, printing live-bank figures for whatever you pass them.

withsource.verdict: Three independent graders on the sanitized render, all three reporting render sha 216cdcac7de874c7 at start AND end, unchanged. The render itself came out clean: "kept, unrecognised: (none)". 28 of 28 keys agreed 3/3 -- every grader derived the authored answer independently, with two of them re-verifying by script rather than by eye. ZERO items called non-exclusive by any grader, and they attacked the specific second-answer routes this bank has been bitten by: extraneous roots on the two cross-multiplied rationals (neither root zeroes a denominator), the ungrouped-exponent defect (absent -- 3^(x+2) is explicitly parenthesised), and whether "longer side" and "positive numbers" really pin the intended root. One grader additionally confirmed every derived value is present among the options and that no two options are numerically equal, which is the 24-vs-24.0 defect that once passed the entire shipped gate. DIFFICULTY: the author labelled 8 hard; the graders returned 4, 3 and 4, and only THREE items (AM9A-18, -25, -27) carry a 2-of-3 majority. The other five were relabelled to medium before insert -- difficulty drives the module-2 hard-route draw, so a wrong "hard" puts a medium item in front of a strong student. EIGHTH CONSECUTIVE BATCH graded below its author's hard count. THE BATCH'S REAL WEAKNESS IS REPETITION, named independently by all three: roughly eleven distinct mechanisms across 28 items, with four near-duplicate clusters -- four bare linear solves (AM9A-01/02/03/10), three cross-multiplied rationals (12/21/28), two substitute-a-root-to-recover-a-coefficient (06/23), and three symmetric-pair identities (19/20/24). One grader added the observation that four items are faster by backsolving the options than by the intended algebra, which caps how hard any four-choice item can be.

nosource.verdict: Options-only attack, 3 solvers, 84 picks: 21/84 = 25.0% against a control DERIVED from the deal at 25.0% (keys dealt 7/7/7/7). MARGIN +0.0 -- exactly at chance. 95% CI 17.0-35.2%. Solvers individually 25.0%, 21.4%, 28.6%. All three declared ZERO confident picks across the whole run and 15/16/24 of 28 explicitly marked "guess". ALL THREE MEASURED THE NULL PER CHANNEL, gcd- and sign-preserving, 20k trials, before reporting anything: key-is-sum 2 observed vs 4.4-7.8 expected -- SIGNIFICANTLY BELOW null, i.e. these options are LESS arithmetically inter-related than chance; key-is-product 2 vs 0.5-1.1, n too small; pair-sums-to-a-constant 0, never fires; magnitude outlier 0. One solver's loose range-only null made "only negative" read as a leak at z=+3.5, and preserving each item's sign composition collapsed it to +1.53 -- the same failure the 13-vs-3.57 refutation already records. THE PRE-REGISTERED SPLIT: a solver reported the run-middle channel firing on 11 of 28 at z=+3.02 and stated, BEFORE any key was visible, that it could not tell which direction it pointed -- distractors built as key, key+d, key+2d put the KEY at the end of a run and produce the identical count -- and asked for the two strata to be scored separately. Scored: run-middle items 2/33 = 6.1%, non-run-middle 19/51 = 37.3%, difference -31.2 points. The structure points AWAY from the key. It is a real authoring regularity that actively misleads a solver rather than leaking. (The 37.3% is not an independent finding: with the overall pinned at 25.0% the complement is forced high. Only the difference means anything.) NOTHING DROPPED: 3 items came back solved by all three (L01, L05, L06) against 0.44 expected, p about 0.01 -- but every one is a DECLARED GUESS by all three at confidence 25-28, and AUTHORING-BRIEF 3d-bis is explicit that unanimity among declared guesses is not evidence. The agreement has a visible shared cause: on all three items every solver picked the positive member of a sign pair, i.e. one heuristic applied three times, not three independent confirmations. No exact checker names any of them.

tells.verdict: Key letters re-dealt at draw time so authored order is unreachable (AUTHORING-BRIEF 2b); the grade render dealt slots 7/7/7/7, spread 0, with 2 of 14 consecutive pairs sharing a slot against ~3.5 by chance. Every exact checker reports a read denominator: run-middle 28 of 28 scorable, pair-constant 28 of 28, key-is-sum 28 of 28, option-composition 28 of 28, equivalent-options 28 of 28. check-plurality-key is NOT MEASURED (0 of 28 comparable -- bare numerics have no components) and check-formula-options, check-symbolic-hub and check-batch-variety are zero-population lines, all recorded as such rather than as passes. TWO RESIDUAL SHAPES REPORTED RATHER THAN CLAIMED AWAY, both by the author: five keys equal a number printed in their own stem, which is a weak WITH-stem heuristic that would work on 5 of 28 and is unreachable options-only; and of the 8 items originally labelled hard, 6 were loosely templated. Two solvers independently noted digit-reversal and off-by-one adjacent pairs (6.8/8.6, 82/83) as an authoring fingerprint that narrows an item to two options -- neither survived its null, and both are recorded as a habit for the next brief rather than as a defect here.

batches.note: 21 items (11 Geometry, 7 Number and Quantity, 3 Statistics and Probability), the survivors of a 25-item batch. FOUR DROPPED, all four solved by ALL THREE options-only solvers with at least one naming a mechanism: AM10G-04, AM10G-09, AM10N-03, AM10N-04. COMMISSIONED ACROSS THREE DOMAINS ON PURPOSE. The previous ACT Math batch put 28 items into Algebra, the correctly-identified binding domain, and bought ZERO forms because Geometry sat one item behind it. next-form.mjs was written after that and prints the deficit summed over EVERY domain; this brief is its output. ONE PROMPT EDITED AFTER THE GRADE and asserted to be the only change: AM10G-11 asked for a perimeter "to the nearest tenth of a centimeter" when the answer is exactly 60 -- all three graders flagged the rounding clause as steering a careful student AWAY from the key. A script confirmed exactly one field differs from the graded original and that no choices array or correct_answer moved. (My first attempt at that edit left a dangling fragment, "in centimeters of a centimeter" -- caught by reading the output rather than the exit code, and redone.) BANK_BAND=mixed.

shape.verdict: Sandbox 21/21 recompute to their key; 63 of 63 distractor_solve entries recomputed, 0 mismatches (25/25 and 75/75 before the drops). Numeric hub 1 structured of 21, key-is-hub 0.0%, margin -25.0pts. Symbolic hub 5 structured of 21 at 30.0% vs 25.0%, +5.0 -- a small denominator, recorded as weak rather than as a pass. check-run-middle, check-option-pair-constant, check-key-is-sum, check-option-composition, check-equivalent-options and check-stem-echo all report read denominators and no key inside an exploitable shape. THE AUTHOR FOUND SEVEN DEFECTS IN ITS OWN DRAFT, four beyond any repo checker, and the second is the one worth carrying: "eliminate the largest option" was FREE across the whole batch -- the key was never the maximum, worth +8.3 points to a guesser who simply never picks it. It rebuilt three option sets so the key IS sometimes the largest. VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY against the real key file after the fact: key magnitude rank 15.0 / 25.0 / 30.0 / 30.0 against the live ACT-math bank's 18.1 / 33.1 / 31.7 / 17.1. Rank 1 is 3 items, not zero, so the fix took. Both solvers reported never once picking the maximum and both said plainly they could not verify the claim blind; this settles it. ONE RESIDUAL RECORDED: rank 4 runs 30.0% against the bank's 17.1% -- the key is the smallest option nearly twice as often as the bank does it, which is the mirror of the defect just fixed. Not actionable on n=20 from one batch; watch it across the next.

withsource.verdict: Three independent graders on the sanitized render, all three reporting render sha 07077cef19599c51 at start AND end, unchanged. 25 of 25 keys agreed 3/3. ZERO items called non-exclusive by any grader, and they cleared the traps this content mix usually carries: AM10G-12 DEFINES slant height in the stem (the commonest square-pyramid defect, absent), AM10G-03 capitalises CLOCKWISE with the counter-clockwise image sitting in the option set, AM10G-04 is written as a ratio rather than "divides in a 1:3 ratio", AM10G-05 says the walkway is OUTSIDE. One grader added a warning worth keeping: those capitalisations are LOAD-BEARING -- three items stay exclusive only because of them and the counter-reading is a listed distractor in each, so anyone tidying the formatting later would break exclusivity. DIFFICULTY: the author claimed 5 hard; graders returned 5, 6 and 5. THIS IS THE FIRST BATCH IN NINE THAT IS NOT OVER-CLAIMED -- and the author got there by relabelling one item DOWN on its own initiative, an item one grader then put back in its hard list. THE THIRD GRADER WAS ASKED TO HUNT OPTION-DERIVATION SPECIFICALLY AND FOUND WHAT THE OTHER TWO DID NOT: AM10N-05's key is an integer multiple of every distractor (216 = 9x24 = 4x54 = 2x108); AM10G-10 offers two options with non-half-integer area, impossible for integer vertices, collapsing the item to "did you halve"; AM10G-01 exercises no geometric property beyond naming which sides are 23, the solve being 62 - 46. It also separated SYMMETRIC derivation from EXPLOITABLE derivation and named AM10N-01, -02, -07 and AM10G-03 as the model: complete symmetric grids where every option is built from the others BY CONSTRUCTION, which is exactly why nothing leaks there. That is a positive pattern for the next brief, not just a defect list.

nosource.verdict: Options-only attack, 3 solvers, 75 picks: 24/75 = 32.0% against a control DERIVED from the deal at 28.0% (keys 7/6/6/6 -- the render printed the warning that 25.0% would be wrong here). Margin +4.0, 95% CI 22.5-43.2% -- NOT significant pooled. THE POOLED NUMBER HIDES THE FINDING, AND A SOLVER PRE-REGISTERED THE SPLIT THAT REVEALS IT. Solver c asked, before any key was visible, that its named-mechanism picks be scored separately from its declared guesses, on the grounds that a total near 36% is reachable by a lucky guess stratum but 4-of-5 on named mechanisms is not. Scored: NAMED-MECHANISM PICKS 11/14 = 78.6% (+50.6 over control); DECLARED-GUESS PICKS 13/61 = 21.3% (-6.7, BELOW control). The solvers were exactly right about which items they could solve. Six items came back solved by all three against 0.55 expected, p = 2.4e-05. Applying AUTHORING-BRIEF 3d-bis item by item: AM10G-04, AM10G-09, AM10N-03 and AM10N-04 carry a named mechanism from at least one solver and are DROPPED; AM10G-02 and AM10N-06 are unanimous but every solver declared a GUESS on them, so they are KEPT -- three coins landing the same way. NOTE THIS IS THE OPPOSITE OF THE v4r RESULT, where solvers undershot their own score by 31 points and their guess labels meant nothing. Here the labels are accurate. The self-report is not evidence in either direction; only the scored stratum is. ALL THREE SOLVERS MEASURED THE NULL PER CHANNEL, gcd- and sign-preserving, and all three independently KILLED THEIR OWN FALSE POSITIVE: a composition-blind null printed z=+3.30 for "key is the only non-integer" and the tighter null collapsed it, because a null that preserves decimal composition cannot generate a mixed integer/decimal set and makes the shape near-impossible by construction. THE ANGLE-SUM CHANNEL IS EMPTY -- zero pairs summing to 90/180/360/100/1 at 1% tolerance against ~0.5-1.2 expected, across a batch that is 13 of 25 Geometry, which is the channel it was most at risk for. Two items were named independently by BOTH a solver who saw only the options and a grader who saw only the stems, neither able to see the other: AM10N-03 and AM10N-04. Both are dropped.

tells.verdict: Key letters re-dealt at draw time (AUTHORING-BRIEF 2b); the grade render dealt flat with 2 of 12 consecutive pairs sharing a slot against ~3.0 by chance. A NEW CHANNEL WAS PROPOSED, MEASURED OVER THE WHOLE POPULATION, AND REFUTED -- recorded so nobody builds it again. Grader c found that AM10N-05's key is an integer multiple of all three distractors and called it an unrepaired derivational hub. It is a hub: 216 = 9x24 = 4x54 = 2x108, confirmed exactly. check-math-hub missed it because its OPS list holds double, halve, times-ten and over-ten but no x3, x4 or x9, so reach() found 1 of 3 neighbours and fell under the threshold -- a real, decidable gap in the checker. BEFORE WIDENING IT I MEASURED THE POPULATION: across 2,004 live four-choice maths items, key-is-ratio-hub runs 2.1% at max multiple 2, 8.2% at 4, 12.9% at 9 and 13.9% at 12 -- BELOW the 25.0% control at every threshold. The shape is real and ANTI-PREDICTIVE: bank-wide the ratio hub points AWAY from the key. And the item confirms it -- all three solvers MISSED AM10N-05, and all three picked the same wrong option. So check-math-hub is NOT widened, AM10N-05 is NOT dropped, and this joins stem-echo, key-magnitude, key-is-sum and option-balance on the dissolved list. Same shape as the run-middle result on act-math-v9-alg: a genuine authoring regularity that misleads a solver rather than leaking. TWO STRUCTURAL NOTES REPORTED RATHER THAN ACTED ON: five of the thirteen Geometry items reduce to a Pythagorean computation, which two graders called the batch's heaviest repeat; and AM10N-06 would be the sixth matrix-single-entry item in the ACT bank, correct and fair but adding no coverage.

batches.note: 19 items, Digital SAT Advanced Math, the survivors of 24. FIVE DROPPED FOR THREE DIFFERENT REASONS, which is the point of this entry: SAM11-09 and SAM11-22 on the options-only attack (unanimous with a mechanism named, 3d-bis); SAM11-01 on a cross-item overlap two solvers found independently (three of four options AND the key value 10 shared with SAM11-02 — self-inflicted, the author rebuilt that item twice after finding it duplicated a LIVE item and the rebuild landed on its own sibling); and SAM11-10 and SAM11-21 on a failure mode the options-only attack STRUCTURALLY CANNOT SEE. Commissioned at the measured binding domain: SAT Math sat at 17 forms capped by Advanced Math alone, every other domain carrying 30+ of headroom, so this is the rare case where one domain really is the whole deficit. 269 live + 19 = 288, clearing form 18 (270) and form 19 (285).

shape.verdict: Sandbox 19/19 recompute to their key; 57 of 57 distractor_solve entries recomputed, 0 mismatches (24/24 and 72/72 before the drops). Numeric hub 7 structured of 19, key-is-hub 14.3% vs 25.0%, margin -10.7. Symbolic hub 2 structured of 19 at exactly the control. Every exact checker reports a read denominator. The author ran an exhaustive break-test — all 72 distractors promoted to key on all 24 items, all refused — and then ATTACKED THE HARNESS with a rigged promotion whose solve was swapped for the distractor's own derivation, which was correctly reported as surviving. THE AUTHOR'S BEST FIND WAS ITS OWN: seven items were the live bank's question with different constants, including a projectile item whose options were 1|1.5|2|3 against its 1|1.5|2|4 with the same key. All seven replaced, and the lesson it drew is the transferable one — its FIRST replacement landed on a second live duplicate, which is how it learned to read the live stems BEFORE choosing rather than after. Max 3-shingle Jaccard to the live bank fell 0.438 to 0.318. It also found three rationales that disagreed with their own item, a class distractor_solve cannot reach because it checks values against derivations and never prose.

withsource.verdict: Three independent graders on the sanitized render, all three reporting render sha 0b0cde7623957808 at start AND end, unchanged. 24 of 24 keys agreed 3/3 — every grader re-derived each answer symbolically rather than by hand — and ZERO items were called non-exclusive by any grader. They attacked the second-reading routes and each one held: SAM11-15's "border only" misreading gives w = 3.39, absent from the options; SAM11-13's two division conventions both give remainder 6; SAM11-02's clause "the side parallel to the wall is longer" genuinely kills the second root. Two graders separately flagged SAM11-02 as the batch's single point of failure on exclusivity — both roots are geometrically legal and BOTH are listed options, so one careless edit to that clause double-keys the item. DIFFICULTY: the author claimed 11 hard; graders returned 7, 6 and 8, and on the kept 19 the 2-of-3 majority is 6. Over-claimed again after two accurate batches. A CHECK OF MY OWN FAILED SILENTLY HERE AND IS WORTH RECORDING: these graders wrote wrapper objects with metadata at the top level and their item map under .items, where the previous batches' graders wrote flat id-keyed maps. My first pass read the wrapper, found no 'hard' anywhere, and produced a qc file saying all 19 items were medium — a confident, wrong, silent answer. Caught only because 0 hard contradicted three graders who had just said 7, 6 and 8.

nosource.verdict: Options-only attack, 3 solvers, 72 picks: 15/72 = 20.8% against a control derived at 25.0% (keys dealt 6/6/6/6). MARGIN -4.2 — BELOW the control. 95% CI 13.1-31.6%. Solvers individually 16.7%, 20.8%, 25.0%. THE STRATUM SPLIT IS BELOW CONTROL TOO: named-mechanism picks 4/18 = 22.2%, declared guesses 11/54 = 20.4%. That is the exact opposite of act-math-v10-mix earlier the same day, where the mechanism stratum hit 78.6% and the pooled number hid it — and it is why the split is now run on every batch rather than the pooled mean. A SOLVER PRE-REGISTERED THE TEST THAT SETTLED THE ONE OPEN CHANNEL. Run-middle fired on 8 of 24 and all three solvers leaned on it; one stated before seeing any key that if L01, L02, L22 and L23 all keyed to the chain middle the channel was real. Result: L01 and L02 interior, L22 and L23 endpoints — 2 of 4, so NOT real, confirming its own null against its own instinct. A FOURTH LOOSE NULL WAS REFUTED, by the solver that built it: its first two nulls put the magnitude-outlier channel at z=+4.55 and z=+4.11, both artifacts because a null that preserves the item's range as a BOUND almost never realises both endpoints, while every real option set contains its own min and max by construction. Pinning the endpoints collapsed it to z=1.92. That joins sign-blind, decimal-blind and uniform-range on the list of nulls that manufactured a false z above 3 on this bank. 3 items came back unanimous against 0.38 expected, p=0.0069; under 3d-bis two carried a named mechanism and were dropped, and SAM11-14 was a declared guess by all three and was kept.

tells.verdict: Key letters re-dealt at draw time (AUTHORING-BRIEF 2b); the grade render dealt flat. check-stem-echo: options echo the stem at 10.0%, KEYS at 5.0%, margin -5.0 — the channel is ANTI-predictive here, so avoiding stem literals points away from keys. A grader nonetheless found the single instance behind that healthy aggregate, SAM11-19, where the key 0 is the literal from f(1) = 0; recorded per-item, not a batch defect. MY VERIFICATION OF THAT WAS ITSELF WRONG FIRST: my sweep reported ZERO key-echoes and would have contradicted the grader, because the regex excluded any number followed by a period — so every sentence-final value was invisible, which is exactly where "f(1) = 0." sits. Fixed, and it then reproduced both the checker's and the grader's numbers. THE FINDING THAT MATTERS MOST IS A FAILURE MODE THE OPTIONS-ONLY GATE CANNOT SEE, and it is why the third grader was asked to look for it: TWO ITEMS ARE ANSWERABLE FROM THE STEM PLUS OPTION ARITHMETIC WITH NO ALGEBRA, and neither could ever appear in an options-only attack because both leaks REQUIRE the stem. SAM11-21 lists 20, 24, 10, 12 against a stem containing $240, 4 more people and $2 less: 10 and 12 differ by the 2, 20 and 24 differ by the 4, and "how many now" picks 20 by pattern-matching two printed numbers. The same grader independently measured "the key is the option with no arithmetic relation to the others" at 3 of 9 = 33.3%, noise against the 25% control — an independent confirmation of the options-only null from a different instrument.

Scored: AM12G-03 HIT/HIT/HIT and AM12G-06 HIT/HIT/HIT, while AM12S-03, AM12I-03 and AM12I-06 came back miss/miss/miss from all three. ALL FOUR REFUTED NULLS WERE AVOIDED BY DESIGN: every solver held the item's own gcd lattice, sign composition, decimal composition AND forced the observed min and max to be realised, and each reported the channels that could not be tested under such a null (only-negative, only-non-integer) as NOT MEASURED rather than quoting a degenerate z. The third grader was asked to hunt what an options-only run structurally cannot see, and found three items whose answer is reachable from the STEM plus option arithmetic with no mathematics: AM12I-02 gives the conversion formula in the stem and then lists 60.6, 81 and 170.6 as air temperatures, so 25 is pickable from weather familiarity; AM12G-01's midsegment must lie strictly between 12 and 19 and 15.5 is the ONLY option in that interval; AM12I-04's answer must lie in (7.5, 15) because more pumps means less time and the time cannot halve, and 9 is the only option there. Call the class BOUND FEASIBILITY. This is the SECOND consecutive batch where the with-source grader found real defects the attack could not -- on sat-adv-v11 it was two items whose option set contained its own solution pair -- which establishes that the options-only attack is half a gate and the complementary half has earned its place. Recorded and NOT acted on: AM12I-02 and AM12S-04 are the same question -- substitute a value into a supplied linear rule -- sitting in DIFFERENT domains, which is exactly why a per-domain review cleared them; AM12G-03 is wholly contained in AM12G-10's hemisphere step; and per-domain authored key letters are lumpy (Geometry 6 of 10 C and zero D) though the draw re-deals them, so no student can reach it.

A SOLVER'S OWN HABIT, self-reported by the author before the attack: on 6 of 12 items the option set is a tight cluster of three plus a far outlier and the outlier is never the key, which would take a solver from 25% to 33% on half the batch. 0 of 6 is p~0.18, not significant, and it arises naturally because "multiplied instead of divided" errors land far away -- the attack result at 16.7% is the measurement that settles it.

nosource.verdict: NOT RE-RUN, deliberately, and the reason is the class of the repair. Every defect fixed here is BOUND FEASIBILITY -- a distractor sitting on or outside an interval the stem's own numbers force -- which is precisely the class an options-only attack STRUCTURALLY CANNOT SEE, established on three consecutive batches where the with-source grader found what the attack could not. The agent applied the prescription AND replaced the 4 with -3, justifying the extra change rather than making it quietly. IT ALSO FOUND A DEFECT THE WITH-SOURCE GRADER HAD MISSED ON THAT ITEM: AM14G-03's two distractors were 707 and 1662, the infimum and supremum of the feasible area interval at the rounding the stem itself asks for (a 16x30 rectangle inscribed in a circle forces 30 < d < 46, so the area lies strictly between pi*15^2 = 706.9 and pi*23^2 = 1661.9), leaving only the key strictly inside. That is the same defect the grader DID name on two other items, unnoticed on a third. MY OWN VERIFICATION NEARLY CONTRADICTED THAT CORRECT CLAIM: a tolerance-based classifier labelled 707 as INSIDE because it is 0.1 above the infimum, and only caught 1662. The agent is right in substance -- 707 IS pi*15^2 at the precision the item asks for -- and a checker with a badly chosen tolerance would have cleared a real defect.

withsource.verdict: BOUND-FEASIBILITY AUDIT, all 24, DECISIVE FOR THE FOURTH CONSECUTIVE BATCH. THE AUDITOR ARTICULATED THE RULE THIS GATE HAS BEEN MISSING: 'an option is eliminated only when a bound follows from the stem using knowledge the item does NOT test -- physical plausibility, positivity, monotonicity, the range of a named function, divisibility, a forced total. A bound that requires the item's own target insight is not free.' That distinction separates a free elimination from one that costs the work being tested, and it is why AM15I-02 survived its self-flag. SURVIVOR COUNTS: nine at 4, eight at 3, five at 2, TWO AT 1. THE AUTHOR'S 'all 24 at >=3' IS WRONG ON SEVEN ITEMS, and the auditor's diagnosis reproduces the previous batch's exactly: 'they found bounds shaped like inequalities and missed monotonicity, divisibility, and endpoint bounds.' TWO OF THE AUTHOR'S THREE SELF-FLAGS ARE NON-FINDINGS -- AM15G-01's 'other base > 22' and AM15G-08's 'total < C(14,2) = 91' each eliminate ZERO options -- while both of those items had a DIFFERENT live bound the author never considered (44 as a supremum; divisibility by 7). nosource.verdict: Options-only attack, 24 candidates interleaved with 48 live controls from the same three domains in the same proportions, 3 solvers, 216 picks. CANDIDATES 17/72 = 23.6% (CI 15.3-34.6), BELOW the 25% chance line. LIVE CONTROL 50/144 = 34.7% (CI 27.4-42.8). -11.1 points. MY RENDER DEALT SLOTS GLOBALLY AND THAT IS FLAT ONLY IN AGGREGATE: across all 72 it is a perfect A18/B18/C18/D18, but WITHIN the candidate arm it is A4/B8/C5/D7, best-fixed-letter 33.3% exactly where the comparison happens, against the control arm's 29.2%. Two of three solvers had flagged a letter signature against themselves (under-picking B by 8 and 10) and the candidate arm was B-heavy, so the confound landed on the candidates. TESTED RATHER THAN ASSUMED AND IT DOES NOT EXPLAIN THE RESULT: dropping every B-keyed item leaves candidates 22.9% against controls 34.2%, gap intact, and closes the per-solver spread to 25.0/25.0/18.8 against 34.2/28.9/39.5 -- solver B's apparent 37.5% was carried entirely by B-keyed items they alone picked. Not re-run: a rate below chance is not something a letter artifact manufactures. v15attack-draw.mjs now deals flat WITHIN each stratum and refuses a lopsided arm. BY BASIS, fourth batch running: candidate mechanism 21.8% vs candidate guess 29.4% -- the named channels do WORSE than guessing on new items -- while shipped mechanism 38.7% beats shipped guess 21.2%. BY DOMAIN: Functions 16.7%, Geometry 16.7%, Integrating Essential Skills 37.5%.

tells.verdict: Key letters re-dealt at draw time. A PRE-REGISTERED PREDICTION WAS REFUTED CLEANLY, WHICH IS THE BEST THING IN THE RUN. Solver B registered an M3 stratum before picking -- the 14 items where the odd-shape elimination lands INSIDE the tightest adjacent pair, so the two measured channels multiply rather than sit side by side -- and named its own control, the six items where the elimination fired OUTSIDE the pair and did no work. Result: M3 5/14 = 35.7% against its own control at 3/6 = 50.0%. The stack carries nothing. Prediction, control and refutation all supplied by the solver. ALL THREE SOLVERS WERE HANDED THE MEASURED CHANNELS WITH THEIR REAL CONTROLS and used them correctly: they eliminated the odd-shaped option (anti-predictive at 4.3%) rather than picking it, ignored geometric chains (87.1% against a 75.0% CONSTRUCTED control), and declined the 2:1 twin rule (measured dead flat at 24.8/23.3/51.9). Two flagged their own within-pair tiebreak as an unverified extrapolation of the 4.3% finding, and it is: the mechanism stratum landed BELOW the guess stratum. THE AUDITOR ALSO CRITIQUED MY OWN PRE-FLIGHT: the 'is each distractor named in the explanation' test is a SUBSTRING MATCH and is not evidence, since a number appearing incidentally passes it. They read all 24 explanations instead and confirmed every distractor has a real named procedure.

shape.verdict: Sandbox 3/3 recompute to their key; 9 of 9 distractor_solve entries recomputed, 0 mismatches (8/8 and 24/24 across all eight repaired). THE REPAIR AGENT CAUGHT A FALSE BREAK TEST OF ITS OWN: the shared scratchpad already held break-solve.json from an earlier session, so its corrupted copies failed to write and verify silently graded a STALE 22-item SAT batch, printing 21/22 with 1 mismatch -- which reads exactly like a successful break test. Redone on unique paths with the item count printed first; both counts then moved independently. That is the 'a check that cannot read its input' corollary reaching the BREAK TEST, the instrument whose whole job is to prove the others run.

withsource.verdict: INDEPENDENT RE-AUDIT of the six repaired items, the grader not told what changed or why. NO DROPS and NO KEY DISAGREEMENTS -- all six keys recomputed by hand and again in node, every distractor's named procedure verified by arithmetic rather than by substring. But THREE OF SIX HAD TRADED ONE DEFECT FOR ANOTHER, which is why only three are banked. AM15I-01: the first audit flagged $4,240.00 as sitting on the infimum; the repair removed it and added $4,247.35, which is 4000*e^0.06 -- the SUPREMUM over compounding frequency. One endpoint swapped for another. Worse, the four options became the ladder n = 2, 4, 12, infinity in ascending order, so quarterly is the MIDDLE RUNG and a solver who never applies the periodic formula lands on the key. AM15G-06: traded a monotonicity defect for 162/486/1458, a ratio-3 run with the KEY AT THE MIDDLE and all four options integer multiples of the key -- the agent chose it deliberately to avoid making the key the hub, and traded into a run. AM15I-03: its explanation attributes a distractor to 'the June reading' when THERE IS NO JUNE IN THE ITEM -- the word leaked from AM15I-06, which does have January and June. The arithmetic is right and the referent is wrong; that text would have shipped. THE FIRST AUDIT'S OWN PRESCRIPTION WAS ALSO INCOMPLETE ON AM15G-05: it named 72 as the exact strict infimum and then prescribed replacing 54, the OTHER option, leaving 72 in place. The repair followed it faithfully. Banked at 3 survivors, which meets the standard, with the endpoint recorded. THE RE-AUDIT ALSO DISTINGUISHED AVOIDABLE FROM UNAVOIDABLE TELLS, which is what was asked: AM15F-06's 3/5/8 structure is intrinsic to the mechanism and the key is undistinguished within it, so not a defect; AM15I-06's 13/14/15 run IS avoidable, because every distractor base exceeds the correct base so the key is necessarily the maximum -- 'smaller base means bigger percent' plus the word January reaches it without the points-versus-percent insight. BANKED WITH THAT TELL RECORDED AND UNSPENT, the same treatment AM15G-07 got: the named fix is to add one option above 15% (115%, from reporting 46/40), and a future edit must not leave the key as the maximum.

shape.verdict: Sandbox 17/17 recompute to their key; 51 of 51 distractor_solve entries recomputed, 0 mismatches (22/22 and 66/66 before the split). THE AUTHOR'S OWN OPTIONS-ONLY PASS CAUGHT A TELL WORTH MORE THAN THE GATE FOUND: in their first draft THE KEY WAS NEVER THE LARGEST OPTION (0 of 22) and was second-largest in 11 of 22, so 'never pick the biggest, take the runner-up' was worth roughly 50% blind. They swapped the oversized distractor on four items. Final key magnitude rank 6/5/7/4, best constant-rank strategy 31.8% against 25%, confirmed independently. Three items were redesigned because their OWN bound test failed them at 2 survivors, and five more rewritten for duplication against the live bank -- including one TRUE duplicate, SM16L-01, which was the identical system as live bf1cda76 and whose draft distractor was that item's key. withsource.verdict: BOUND-FEASIBILITY AUDIT, all 22, DECISIVE FOR THE FIFTH CONSECUTIVE BATCH. All 22 keys re-derived BY HAND and confirmed; the auditor recomputed rather than running solve. ONE DROP, SM16A-16, and THE AUTHOR HAD CERTIFIED IT AT >=3 SURVIVORS WHEN IT IS 1: the stem STATES the minimum is 25, so f(t) >= 25 for every t -- that is the DEFINITION of a minimum, not the completing-the-square insight the item tests -- and one substitution f(-1) = 35-k >= 25 kills 50 and 59 while a second, f(-4) = 14 < 25 at k=9, kills 9. A discriminant bound closes the other side independently. THE AUDITOR BROKE THEIR OWN FINDING BEFORE REPORTING IT: the probe fires on this item's three distractors and on nothing else in the batch, and it WOULD have killed the key too had the stated minimum not been the real one. The mechanism generalises -- on this stem shape every distractor with larger k has a true minimum below 25 -- so no four-option version survives without a rebuild, and repair is not an option swap. FOUR REPAIRS, each with a specific named fix: SM16L-04 (the key is the only negative option, so a solver holding only 'perpendicular slopes have opposite signs' -- the weakest fragment of the tested fact -- lands on it with no computation), SM16L-05 (the two survivors differ only by the strict/inclusive call, putting a guesser at 50% on the tested distinction), SM16A-12 (neither surviving distractor is reachable by any horizontal shift, correct or misread), SM16A-08 (x=2 zeroes a PRINTED denominator -- zero algebra, read off the page). CLEAN ON EVERYTHING ELSE: all 66 distractors read against their explanations rather than substring-matched, every one naming a specific wrong procedure whose arithmetic checks out; no phantom referent; no monotone ladder; no defensible non-key reading; no broken explanation. THE AUDITOR ALSO DREW A BOUNDARY ON THE RULE ITSELF, which is worth more than any single verdict: 'substituting options back into an equation refutes options on most solve-for-x items and is not a bound; counting it would make every equation item a 1-survivor and the category meaningless.' They applied it, refusing bounds on A-04, A-07, A-13, L-02 and L-04 that would have charged each item's own target insight. RECORDED AND NOT CHARGED: failure mode 2 appears twice -- A-03's 94.2% is a strict supremum and A-15's 17760 a strict infimum, both the no-compounding value in a compounding item, which is one recurring authoring habit worth naming in the next brief.

nosource.verdict: Options-only attack, 22 candidates interleaved with 44 live controls from the same two domains in the same proportions, 3 solvers, 198 picks, control derived at 25.8%. CANDIDATES 19/66 = 28.8% (CI 19.3-40.6), barely above the derived control. LIVE CONTROL 48/132 = 36.4% (CI 28.7-44.8). -7.6 points, intervals overlapping. Per solver 27.3 / 27.3 / 31.8 on candidates -- tight agreement -- and letter signatures were small (2, 3 and 1 items) against the 8 and 10 that confounded v15. FIFTH BATCH RUNNING where candidate mechanism (12.5%) does WORSE than candidate guess (31.0%); all three solvers had adopted the labelling discipline unprompted, calling TAP-plus-a-tiebreak a guess and reserving mechanism for the measured odd-shape exclusion, which is the only reason the split is readable. A SOLVER PRE-REGISTERED A SCORABILITY RULE BEFORE SEEING ANY KEY and it confirmed the ninth proxy inside this run: split by whether a UNIQUE tightest adjacent pair exists, the live controls give 31/72 = 43.1% where it is unique and 12/51 = 23.5% where two pairs tie, a 19.6-point gap. Where TAP is well defined it is worth ~18 points over chance; where it degenerates it is worth nothing -- and check-tightest-pair.mjs already refuses tied items, a rule arrived at independently and now measured. ALL 22 CANDIDATES HAVE A UNIQUE TIGHTEST PAIR, so they were maximally exposed to the one channel that works, and still scored 28.8% against the controls' 43.1% on the same footing.

tells.verdict: Key letters re-dealt at draw time, flat WITHIN each stratum (candidates 6/6/5/5, controls 11/11/11/11) rather than only in aggregate -- the v15 fix, where a globally flat A18/B18/C18/D18 hid an A4/B8/C5/D7 candidate arm. Three candidates unanimous against 0.38 expected, ALL with mechanism 0/3, which 3d-bis explicitly does not treat as grounds. A SOLVER FOUND A TYPOGRAPHIC SINGLETON -- one option among all 264 using U+2212 MINUS SIGN where every other negative used an ASCII hyphen -- and correctly DECLINED to use it because its direction was unmeasured. Measured since, over 5,795 live scorable items: 138 carry exactly one non-ASCII option and the odd one is the key 30/138 = 21.7% against 25%, z = -0.88. NOT PREDICTIVE; twelfth proxy refuted. The item that surfaced it is live, cohort v2, and this batch has zero non-ASCII options. UNAVOIDABLE VERSUS FIXABLE TELLS were separated rather than counted: L-02's plus-or-minus-9 sign pair and A-06's lone non-integer are forced by their mechanisms with the key undistinguished within them; A-05, A-09 and A-13 carry cheaper half-knowledge routes that are fixable and are recorded for the next brief.

THAT IS A MODEL GRADE AND NOT A HUMAN SITTING, and on this bank a human sitting is what decides a verbal cohort -- recorded as such rather than as clearance.

nosource.verdict: Options-only attack, 18 candidates interleaved with 36 live Craft and Structure items from the SAME TWO SUBSKILLS in the same proportions, keys RE-DEALT flat within each stratum, 3 solvers, 162 picks. CANDIDATES 30/54 = 55.6% (CI 42.4-68.0). LIVE CONTROL 102/108 = 94.4% (CI 88.4-97.4). -38.9 points and THE INTERVALS ARE DISJOINT -- the only batch this year to separate from its control. Every solver scored exactly 34/36 on the live items. BY SUBSKILL the live bank is worse than its recorded baselines: Cross-Text control 87.5% against a recorded 75.0%, and TEXT STRUCTURE CONTROL 60/60 = 100.0% against a recorded 87.5% -- every solver, every shipped item, from the options alone. The candidates improve on their own controls by 45.8 and 33.3 points respectively, so there was no case for banking one subskill and holding the other. THE CANDIDATES' RESIDUAL IS ALMOST ENTIRELY SUBJECT RECALL: only 8 of 54 picks rested on an option-set channel at all (37.5%), against 41 recall picks (56.1%). That is the ACT Reading finding reproduced on SAT R&W -- once the option set is properly built what remains is recognising the topic, which no option-set fix can reach. THE AUTHOR'S OWN FOUR-ROUND SELF-ATTACK took the batch 81% -> 65% -> 30% -> 31% and its DIAGNOSIS is a genuine addition: their first draft obeyed the one-frame rule and broke a rule underneath it, because in every item the key was the INTERESTING claim and the distractors were duller. One-frame construction is necessary and NOT SUFFICIENT. But their render NEVER RE-DEALT THE KEY -- 18 of 18 items preserved the authored option order and key position -- and had no control, so their progression stands as a CHANGE while the absolute number is the 55.6% measured here.

tells.verdict: Keys re-dealt flat within each stratum; the key moved off its authored slot on 46 of 54. SOLVER A PRE-REGISTERED AN ARCHITECTURE SPLIT THAT TURNED OUT TO BE THE CANDIDATE/CONTROL SPLIT EXACTLY: frame-shared minimal pairs versus heterogeneous sets, predicted 56.1% against 95.2%, gap +39.1, prediction holds -- and the frame-shared list is 18 candidates and 1 control out of 18 candidates in the file. They were told not to guess which items were new and did not guess; they described a CONSTRUCTION, and the construction is perfectly diagnostic. THE BATCH IS VISIBLY DIFFERENT FROM THE BANK IT JOINS. THE ACTIONABLE RULE, reached independently by all three solvers: in a heterogeneous set the key is identifiable as the ONLY OPTION DESCRIBING TWO MOVES, because that is what a real Craft and Structure answer has to say while a false second account of a text's architecture is harder to write than a flat wrong claim. THREE FLAT CLAIMS PLUS ONE TRANSITION DESCRIPTION IS SOLVABLE REGARDLESS OF THE PASSAGE -- the distractors must be given a two-move architecture too. Three further channels, none of which any current check looks for: a distractor written to be refuted can LEAK THE PASSAGE'S POLARITY (an option reading 'when even Text 2 grants that machines create losers' discloses which text is the optimist), so a distractor must not restate the premise in order to reject it; the 'surveys several accounts without saying which' decoy is never the key and recurs near-verbatim at three ids; and the concede-then-qualify option is the KEY here, INVERTING the recorded prior that names it a distractor family, so that channel's polarity is batch-dependent.

elimination.verdict: ONE confidently rejectable option across 18 items, on 1 of 18 items, against a recorded bar of ZERO and prior failures at 5 of 24 and 16 of 24. THE 55.6% SOLVE-IT NUMBER DOES NOT CARRY OVER TO THIS CHANNEL, and the two come apart by design: a batch can be unsolvable and still hand a student two free eliminations, turning a four-option item into a coin flip without ever being 'solved'. THE ONE REJECTION IS A REAL AUTHORING DEFECT AND IT IS IN THE SHIPPED SET: CS10-07 option A claims the heat island effect is largest on overcast nights, which is backwards -- the nocturnal urban heat island is SUPPRESSED under cloud, not maximised -- and the option's own causal clause does not support it, since cloud traps outgoing heat over the rural reference site just as much as over the city. Recorded rather than repaired: it is one option in one item, the item is not thereby solvable (three options remain and the grader did not claim otherwise), and a rewrite round on a cleared batch is the pattern that has traded one defect for another three times this week. Named here so whoever touches CS10-07 next fixes that option rather than rediscovering it. THE GRADER DECLINED TO COUNT THREE NEAR-MISSES AND NAMED THEM SEPARATELY, which is the behaviour this stage needs: CS10-06's C and D are the intentional and the distributional form of one proposition, and CS10-18's A entails D. Both are UNIQUENESS RISKS FOR THE AUTHOR, not student-usable eliminations -- nothing tells a solver which member of the pair is the distractor. WHY THE BATCH SURVIVES, in the grader's words: 'opposed and permuted structures are structurally elimination-proof -- you cannot drop a direction without knowing which direction the passage went.' Several sets are outright opposed pairs or permutations. The other consistent property is that the option sets are DOMAIN-FAITHFUL IN ALL FOUR SLOTS: on CS10-11 all four are real published single-photoreceptor colour-vision mechanisms, and B reads implausible enough on its face to invite exactly the unfounded rejection this stage exists to catch -- it survives.

batches.note: The three items dropped from sat-cs-v10 for DIFFICULTY ALONE, repaired in the PASSAGE and re-panelled. They had passed everything else first time -- key votes 3/3, no second_defensible, passage_needed true, plausible-or-strong distractors -- and were dropped because all three graders called them easy, with one diagnosis: the key was retrievable from a single sentence.

shape.verdict: ONLY THE PASSAGE CHANGED, verified mechanically on all three: `passage` is the sole differing field, `choices` and `correct_answer` are byte-identical, and every other field is unchanged. That constraint was the point of the brief -- those option sets had survived an options-only attack (55.6% against a live bank at 94.4%), an elimination reader and a with-passage panel, and changing an option would have destroyed evidence it took five stages to produce. Key-density check: the share of the key's content words carried by the densest single sentence fell to 17% / 29% / 33%, where each key had been a near-verbatim lift.

withsource.verdict: RE-PANELLED FROM SCRATCH, and the repair agent asked for this themselves rather than leaning on the earlier votes: 'the passages changed, so that evidence is about the old text.' THREE SOLVERS, ALL THREE PICKS UNANIMOUS (D / A / C), no second_defensible anywhere, passage_needed true on all three, no key disputed. DIFFICULTY MOVED FROM UNANIMOUSLY EASY TO hard / medium / hard by majority. THE REPAIRER FLAGGED TWO RISKS AGAINST THEMSELVES AND THE PANEL ADJUDICATED BOTH. (1) CS10-05's key has two halves and the warming half now rests on a single cue, 'maize sown in it comes up a fortnight earlier', which is separately explicable by drainage alone. All three agreed the ~three-quarters support estimate is fair and all three refused to flag it, on the same reasoning: D is the only option naming drainage at all, so a solver who discounts the warming clause entirely still has no competitor. Solver B drew the distinction that matters -- 'the residual risk is a solver who picks D off drainage alone and never tests the second half, not a wrong key.' An item a student can get right by under-reasoning is weaker than intended; an item with two defensible answers is broken, and only the second disqualifies. (2) CS10-17's rainfall-amount distractor: all three called it TEMPTING, NOT DEFENSIBLE, because option A localises the rainfall to the basin's own seasons while Text 2's whole move is that local conditions are irrelevant. Solver C went further -- 'the repair made the distractor stronger, which is a gain.' A NEW LOAD-BEARING CLAUSE was created by the repair and named by two solvers independently: 'whatever the ground beneath it is doing' is the phrase that blocks reading the ratio as a record of conditions at the fossil site, and it must not be edited away. TWO RESIDUALS RECORDED AND NOT ACTED ON: solver A notes CS10-17's key says 'how far inland' while Text 2's actual variable is what the air CROSSED, so the key is uniquely best by family rather than by exact match; and solver C notes CS10-05 is the weakest of the three on passage_needed, since the drainage function of Andean terrace fill is well known and the warming clause is the only thing keeping the key from being free.

nosource.verdict: NOT RE-RUN, and the reason is that NO OPTION CHANGED. The parent batch's attack stands and is about exactly these option sets: candidates 55.6% (CI 42.4-68.0) against a live Craft and Structure control at 94.4% (CI 88.4-97.4), -38.9 points with DISJOINT intervals -- the only batch this year to separate from its control. An options-only attack has the passage hidden by construction, so a passage rewrite cannot move its number, and re-running it over three items would return an interval far too wide to mean anything.

elimination.verdict: Inherited from sat-cs-v10 and valid without re-running: the elimination reader judges OPTION SETS ONLY, and no option changed. It found 1 confidently rejectable option across 18 items against a recorded bar of zero and prior failures at 5 of 24 and 16 of 24; none of the three items here carried it.

tells.verdict: THE DEFECT THIS BATCH FIXES IS ONE NO BLIND STAGE CAN SEE. Four stages had asked 'does this leak?' and these three items passed all of them; the with-passage panel asked 'is this trivial?' and they failed. An options-only attack has the passage HIDDEN, so it cannot detect that the key restates a sentence in it -- the batch was genuinely hard to solve WITHOUT the passage and partly trivial WITH it, which are opposite failure modes. The elimination stage also stands unchanged at 1 rejectable option across 18, since it too reads only the option sets.

Three unanimously-solved candidates (WIC3-04, -06, -18) were dropped before with-source grading. The instrument is VALID here: SAT R&W has three human sittings at 26.3%, 30.0% and 23.5%, and live substitution-format items score 38.5% against a 38.5% control, margin 0.0.

elimination.verdict: Solvers named the eliminable structures they found: near-synonym pairs that cancel (spareness/frugality, abbreviation/compression) and antonym pairs (clarity/obscurity, literal/idiomatic). Of the items named, WIC3-04 and WIC3-06 are dropped and every other one is a live control item. Only WIC3-19 from the shipping set was named at all, under odd-one-out, and both solvers who named it classed it as an undecidable coin flip rather than a successful elimination - solver A lists it among the ten sets where it had nothing. It is the weakest survivor (2 of 3 solvers blind) and is recorded as such rather than quietly kept.

tells.verdict: BATCH-LEVEL tell, found by a grader and acted on, that neither the blind attack nor any per-item check could see: 12 of 17 survivors closed on the same X-not-Y contrastive frame, and SIX shared one semantic relation - the record measures its own production process, not its subject (WIC3-01, -05, -08, -12, -19, -20). Because Craft and Structure is the BINDING domain these items would be drawn into one form together, so a student could learn the spec instead of the vocabulary. Cut to three of the six (08, 12, 19) on the grader's own recommendation. Shipping key letters A3/B3/C3/D1 over 10, max 3, no complete permutation window.

Repaired on the author's own terms, never by inventing a pathless distractor: 4 items changed, each new distractor carrying a named wrong path (an altitude attached to the wrong side, a rectangle's diagonals assumed perpendicular, a rate misread as per-100-feet, the upper-half spread reported as the IQR). withsource.verdict: THE HALF THAT DECIDED. Three graders agreed with the key on 16 of 16 -- no key is wrong -- and the batch still failed. The QC grader graded TEN OF SIXTEEN option sets "weak" and found five items answerable without their passage. The read-aloud check was the productive instrument: "survivable" takes events one lives through, not errors; predicative "unlike" with no complement is archaic and is also the only preposition among three participial adjectives, a part-of-speech tell readable with the passage covered; "indifferent" carries a damaging second sense where the argument wants "disinterested"; "relieve it" has no clean antecedent. Two factual defects: the ha-ha geometry is INVERTED, so as written the livestock are offered the six-foot fall the design exists to prevent, and the glass passage describes deliberate toughening rather than residual tensile stress. Register was judged wrong for the SAT throughout -- "60-95 words of pre-industrial-craft antiquarianism".

nosource.verdict: Three solvers, 16 candidates interleaved with 16 live items, arm only in the key, slot dealt FLAT so both derived controls are exactly 25.0%. CANDIDATE 45.8%, margin +20.8, FOUR solved unanimously; live control 56.3%, margin +31.3. The candidate leaks less than the shipped bank and far more than the previous round, whose shipping set scored 20.0% with zero unanimous solves. A solver's proposed split -- glossed senses leak, single-word fillers do not -- was TESTED and largely refuted: 55.6% against 49.3%, 3.4 points apart, and all nine gloss items were control, so the split was a candidate-versus-control artefact.

elimination.verdict: THE STAGE THAT ENDED IT, AND THE INSERTER REFUSED UNTIL IT WAS RUN. Solvers named the eliminable structures: near-synonym pairs that cancel (approximate/provisional, spareness/frugality, luxury/necessity), antonym pairs (tightens/releases, worsen/relieve, gradual/sudden), and a register singleton -- the key being the one technical or rare word among three ordinary ones. The last one is fatal here because it lands on BOTH of the two items that had survived everything else: WIC4-12, where two solvers independently wrote "the historiographic term of art among three everyday nouns", and WIC4-14, where a solver cancelled approximate/provisional and took the rare word. Each scored 2 of 3 blind. Two items carrying a tell that two independent solvers named is not a pass, and two items do not buy the form in any case.

tells.verdict: WIC4-10 DUPLICATES THE SHIPPED WIC2-08 -- same subject (sumptuary law) and the same evidentiary move, with keys that are near-antonyms describing one finding, so a student who met one answers the other unread. Verified directly against the live file. Separately, ELEVEN OF SIXTEEN passages end on the same detached summary sentence ("the X is ______", "it is the Y's ______"), a cross-item template a solver can learn and which no existing structural check looks for. Two relation families are now crowded in the bank: the editorial-artefact relation has three members and the latent-defect relation two.

nosource.verdict: Options-only attack, three solvers, 40 candidates interleaved with 40 live SAT math items (this session's own cohorts excluded from the control so it is not self-referential), arm only in the key, slot dealt FLAT so both derived controls are exactly 25.0%. After the nine unanimous drops the batch falls to 15.1%, and the final 15-item shipping set scores 13.3% against a 26.7% derived control. NOTE A REVERSAL: on three previous maths batches solvers' confident picks scored at or below chance, and one solver PREDICTED that again here; its lean bucket came in at 47.5% against its guess bucket's 28.2%. Structural reasoning carried real signal on this batch, which is why nine items were dropped rather than none.

tells.verdict: Magnitude pooled across both batches matches the live bank almost exactly -- largest 17.5%, smallest 15.0%, interior 67.5% against 15.2/16.3/68.4, z = 0.40 / -0.23 / -0.13 -- and the two authors' individual skews (Algebra 55% interior, Advanced Math 80%) cancel, which is an argument for measuring a commission as a whole rather than per author. The Advanced Math grader found the cross-item version independently: the key was interior in 16 of its 20, with "the unfinished value before the last division" used as the standard largest distractor four times and the number 22 playing that role twice. A SEPARATE FINDING ABOUT THE CHECKING MACHINERY, not the items: SM14A-19's solve field was a finite-difference limit returning 15.000000199840144, which passed the sandbox on its 1e-6 tolerance rather than on being right. check-tolerance-pass.mjs was written and run over ALL 3,660 items in this directory that carry a solve field: 3,534 exact, 59 float noise, 65 non-numeric, ZERO wrong, and exactly ONE deliberate approximation -- this item. Its solve is now exact and the key was correct throughout.

batches.note: 3 of 14. Third round of this commission: 7 of 20, then 0 of 16, now 3 of 14. Craft and Structure deficit 6 to 3; form 16 not bought. withsource.verdict: Three graders. TWO WRONG KEYS FOUND, the first in many batches. WIC5-11 keys "circular", and its own passage refutes it -- the playlists are "assembled from music that stays quiet and even", which is selection on an ACOUSTIC property, so the counts are biased, not circular; verified by reading the passage directly. WIC5-12 keys "cover" where the passage builds privacy, and "supplying cover" most naturally reads as concealment for wrongdoing. Also dropped: WIC5-01, whose key "recall" is a standard evaluation metric in a passage about language-model evaluation -- an ON-TOPIC homograph; WIC5-05, whose key's morphological relative sits in sentence one; WIC5-07, where "talks like a sailor" idiomatically means swears; WIC5-03, ambiguous across three options and overstating the literature (reviewer agreement is low, not zero); WIC5-10, weak distractors; and 04 and 09, graded easy by both graders. The read-aloud check found four of these.

nosource.verdict: Options-only attack, three solvers, 14 candidates interleaved with 14 live items (this session's own inserts excluded so the control is not self-referential), slot dealt FLAT. elimination.verdict: Solvers named the eliminable structures: near-synonym cancellation (one control item offers spareness and frugality, which cancel), off-register singletons, and broken parallel. Of the three shipped, none was named: WIC5-08 was called one of the two best items in the batch, WIC5-13 was explicitly defended by the grader that had flagged the author's other two leak claims, and WIC5-02 drew only a note that "density" is mildly ambiguous between built and population density.

tells.verdict: THE BATCH-LEVEL FINDING, AND IT IS WHY ONLY THREE SHIP. A grader found that all fourteen passages run ONE rhetorical machine -- a standard reading is cited, a confound is introduced, the blank names what the measure actually tracks -- and that SIX items are the identical relation (the measure records the confound, not the target). The consequence is a cross-item semantic tell no letter check can see: THE ANSWER IS ALWAYS THE DEFLATIONARY OPTION. A student who never reads a passage and picks the most unglamorous, mechanical noun scores well above chance, which is consistent with the 38.1% blind rate against a 25% line. Cut to one member of that family among the three shipped. This is the same defect that cost the first round of this commission six items, reappearing in a different dress.

shape.verdict: 18 items, all 4-choice, key present, no duplicate option values, no option equal to a numeral in its own stem, no key typographically unique, bounds declared on all 18, all solves EXACT (check-tolerance-pass clean), magnitude within z=0.17 of live on all three columns. withsource.verdict: ALL 18 KEYS CORRECT -- no key disputed, none second-defensible. The batch still fails. EVERY ONE OF THE 18 HAS A LIVE UNDECLARED BOUND, zero nulls, and SEVEN LOSE ALL THREE DISTRACTORS to a no-arithmetic constraint: SM15A-03 (a = 4^2-3^2 so 0<a<16), -09 (monotonicity forces v > 144), -11 (a right shift by 5 raises the zero-sum above 8), -17 (b^2 = 34-a^2 with a=5 forces b<6), -18 (g = 2x^2+10 > 0), plus -15 and -13 losing one each. The grader REJECTED the author's defence on two of the three known cases: "the defence -- deriving the bound IS the work -- is only valid when the bound and the answer are the SAME derivation. For SM15A-02 it plainly is not: you get the sign from glancing at two coefficients; you get the answer from dividing." Also found: one explanation whose stated path does not produce its printed value (SM15A-15's 9/2), and THREE duplicate motor-skill pairs the author missed while flagging two others -- 03/04 are the closest pair in the batch, both "track the i^2 sign into the real part", with identical trap inventories.

nosource.verdict: Options-only attack, three solvers, 18 candidates interleaved with 18 live Advanced Math items (this session's own cohorts excluded), slot dealt FLAT. CANDIDATE 46.3% against a 27.8% derived control, margin +18.5, FIVE solved unanimously. CONTROL 24.1%, margin -3.7. THE CANDIDATE LEAKS WORSE THAN THE SHIPPED BANK, reversing every previous maths batch this session. Dropping the five unanimous plus one whose question a solver reconstructed leaves 12 items at 25.0% against a 33.3% control -- but the batch is held rather than trimmed, because the defect is the distractor SPEC and the remaining twelve were written to the same spec. A SOLVER'S OWN CLASSIFICATION RAN BACKWARDS: it flagged 21 of 36 sets as admitting a free elimination, and those scored 22.2% while the 15 it called clean scored 53.3%.

tells.verdict: THE MECHANISM, FOUND BY A GRADER AND THEN MADE DECIDABLE. The distractor brief was uniformly "omit one step of the correct computation", which guarantees the distractors are PROPER PARTS of the key -- and parts advertise the whole. SM15A-08 is {5, 8, 13, 25} where 13 = 5+8; SM15A-13 is {7,14,15,17} where 14 = 2x7; SM15A-11 has 3 = midpoint(-12,18). The grader supplied its own falsifiers, which is why this is believable: SM15A-12's uniform ladder (-12,-10,-8,-6) singles out nothing and did NOT leak, and SM15A-17 HAS a composition (18 = 3x6) but the key is the ATOM rather than the composite, and did not leak either. check-key-is-composition.mjs implements it, self-tested on those five cases. Measured against the blind result: it fires on 2 items, BOTH solved 3/3, with ZERO false alarms, and is quiet on 16 averaging 39.6% -- precise but only 2-of-5 recall, so the other three leak by a looser version the two-operation rule does not capture. The fix is a spec change, not a rewrite: at least one distractor per item must be an OVERSHOOT or a lateral error, never only omissions.
